title: Flower paste sweet pea
subtitle: modelling sweet pea flowers in gum paste
excerpt: Sugar sweet peas are made from flower paste (gum paste), which dries to a thin, petal-like rigidity that fondant cannot achieve. Each flower has two components, a ruffled standard petal at the back and two cupped wing petals in front, assembled on a hooked wire. They can be coloured with petal dusts and arranged in cascades on wedding and celebration cakes. This is one of the most achievable wired sugar flowers for a new sugarcraft modeller.
sourceNotes: Sugar floristry, modelling edible flowers from gum paste, is a defined discipline within British sugarcraft with dedicated City and Guilds qualification levels. Sweet peas are a standard first or second wired flower in sugarcraft courses because their construction is relatively simple: two petal shapes rather than the five to seven required for more complex flowers like roses or peonies. Wired sugar flowers are not suitable for direct insertion into cakes served to the public without a floristry cage or card separator, as the wires are not edible. Commercial production of sugar sweet peas appears in wedding cake decoration from at least the 1970s; the design reflects the real flower's bi-layer structure closely.

recipe.batchNotes: Make in batches and store in a box lined with tissue paper for up to 1 month.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Allow at least 48 hours drying time; make well ahead.

content.text: Sugar sweet peas use flower paste (gum paste) rather than fondant because they need to dry rigid and thin. The flower is built on a hooked wire: a ruffled standard petal (the large upright petal) is formed first on the wire, then two cupped wing petals are added in front. Once dry, the flowers are dusted with petal dust to add colour depth and a more realistic look.

items.prepNote: per 5-6 flowers; tinted pale pink, mauve, or white

content.text: Cut 26-gauge floral wire into 10 cm lengths. Bend a small hook at one end of each wire by pressing the top 5 mm back against itself with needle-nose pliers. The hook will anchor the flower paste during assembly.

Roll a small piece of gum paste on a non-stick board to about 1 mm thick. Cut out the standard petal using the larger sweet pea cutter. Place on the foam pad and run a ball tool around the upper edge to thin and ruffle it into soft waves. Moisten the hooked end of a wire with edible glue or water. Press the hook into the lower centre of the standard petal so the hook sits inside the paste. Fold the lower sides of the petal up to cup slightly around the wire. Pinch at the base to secure and hang upside down or support in foam to dry for 30 minutes.

Cut two wing petals with the smaller sweet pea cutter. Thin the edges with the ball tool but keep these less ruffled than the standard, the wings are smooth-cupped. Moisten the base of each wing petal and press one to each side of the wired standard, curving them forward around the wire. The two wings should curve toward each other at the front, nearly meeting in the middle. Secure by pressing the base of each wing firmly to the standard. Leave to dry fully for 48 hours.

Once completely dry, dust the outer edges of the standard and the wing petals with petal dust using a flat brush, deepening the colour toward the edges and leaving the centre lighter. Tape several flowers together with half-width floral tape, starting just below the calyx and winding down the wire stem. Do not insert wired flowers directly into a cake without a food-safe separator.

If the paste cracks when you cup or frill the petals, it has dried too fast or is too stiff. Rub a tiny smear of vegetable shortening into the surface and cover with a polythene bag for a minute to restore pliability. Avoid working gum paste in a warm kitchen, it skins over far more quickly than fondant. If petals won't hold their shape and droop, the paste is too soft: knead in a pinch of extra CMC (tylose) powder and allow a short rest before continuing. Never leave shaped petals uncovered; even a thin film on the surface prevents fine detail from being impressed cleanly.
